question: Does Us. apply its Basic Attack damage bonus by delivered packet category independently of input role?
decision: Interpret native DamageSourceCategory A as Basic Attack. Add the exact T1-T5 ratio in the additive damage-bonus zone for every wearer packet with that category, including delayed off-field packets. Missing or unknown packet categories fail. The effect is permanent; it has no trigger or expiry. Category mapping and packet-time eligibility remain explicit tested hypotheses.
availability: Frozen Global release availability remains unverified.
stop_condition: Check refinement curves/units, legal equipped build, independent damage arithmetic, all supported packet categories, delayed off-field ownership, invalid configurations and CLI/WASM/Worker parity.
return_condition: New packet classification, release or damage-zone evidence conflicts with the model.
checks: 155 content tests pass: exact T1-T5 ratios and changed-parameter/unit rejection, legal Nanally/Us. native build and independently calculated additive damage multiplier.

Packet category/element cross-check: 1000 ATK * .5 DEF * (1 + .1 general + .12 weapon) = 610 for A packets; other categories remain 550. Delayed A delivery after switching remains wearer-only. Duplicate/mismatched gear and missing/unknown packet categories fail.
The Nanally first-attack packet is selected by the native content owner and published through the catalog; this is a partial primary-packet model, not a full ordinary chain or kit.

Public Nanally A0 level 80 talents 8/8/8 equipped Us. T1-T5: attack and skill execute; independent attack multiplier (1 + .1 general + .15 Anima + weapon)/(1 + .1 + .15), unaffected skill, incompatible weapon rejection and full CLI/WASM report equality. Real Worker executes the T5 script and agrees with direct WASM.

TypeScript and production build pass; weapon_passives, native_build and scenario_script modules pass. Command: NTESIM_VERIFY_NATIVE=1 NTESIM_VERIFY_WEAPON=prokaryon node tools/web.mjs test --test tests/weapon_passives.test.mjs tests/native_build.test.mjs tests/scenario_script.test.mjs (from web). Native parity is scoped to the changed weapon; the other weapons retain WASM/Worker checks.

Changed Rust files pass rustfmt. Content clippy passes with only the two existing metadata lints collapsible_if and single_element_loop allowed; unqualified -D warnings still fails on those pre-existing lints.
